Gadjet is makin' me rite this to try improve me spellin' as it's enoyin her. dunno why she xpects an ex-hooligon to spell n rite shit but okay... i love her tho, the silly bitch.

so rite, we lef camden this morn, wagon rattlin off the coblz. trade been decent, got rid o lot o junk, picked up few tickets, not bad fer once. so we figger best move out. london gettin' too heavy wiv pollyticks, too loud, too many peepel wantin summat fer nuthin. time we go see wot's past the wall.

we went all way back down to nelson pole thing. told us no real room to be setting up shop in easty. fella in market say there's place called canter out dere somewhere. sound silly, but maybe true. maybe jest a tale to keep mugs wanderin. dont matter, we need road. road mean fresh folk, fresh purse, fresh bite to eat.

we went all way back again towards top west exit, nobdy relly knows bout dis one. anyways the sun was droppin when we seen it - the beast. swear on mum's grave never seen nuthin so weird as him. big n grey, skin wrinkly like old coat left in rain. nose hang long, swayin side ta side like hosepipe drippin. ears big as bedsheets, flap slow, soft. it dint run, dint bark, dint growl. just stood there, watchin us. eyes half shut, lookin sly, shifty. made me spine cold. like it cud know wot's in yer head, but won't tell. we set up camp next to it. guess it's now our big guard dog hahaha

some o the tommy lads whisper "elefant." dunno the word, but sound right.

we maybe might try take it wiv us... but i aint gonna fight it if it says no! Me and Gadj are gonna keep goin anyway. gotta find canter. maybe canter better. maybe canter worse.
Cinders xoxox

煤渣，亲亲抱抱

Dear Mr. Thistleton,

Thank you for your recent submission regarding your invention, the Railway Rifle. The Ministry has reviewed your proposal with great interest and acknowledges the ingenuity and potential benefits your device might offer in expediting railway maintenance operations.

However, after thorough consideration, we regret to inform you that we must decline the adoption of this invention for official use. The primary concern lies within the domain of health and safety regulations. The Railway Rifle, as described, presents several risks akin to those associated with a high-powered nail gun. Specifically, the risk of accidental discharge, misfiring, or injury from handling such a powerful tool in confined conditions has led to this decision.

While we appreciate the time and effort you have invested in developing this concept, the safety of railway workers must remain our utmost priority. We recommend revisiting the design to include more robust safety features and invite you to resubmit your proposal after addressing these concerns.

Honourable Members of the Ministry,

I am writing to formally present my latest invention, the Railway Rifle, designed specifically to streamline and expedite the process of installing rail spikes into railway sleepers, particularly within the confines of underground tunnels. The device functions by utilising a pneumatic mechanism to accurately and swiftly drive spikes into position, reducing the manual labour and time currently required by traditional methods.

Key features of the Railway Rifle include:

+ Ease of Use: Designed with ergonomics in mind, allowing railway workers to operate it with minimal training.
+ Efficiency: Capable of driving multiple spikes within a fraction of the time taken by existing manual techniques.
+ Precision: Ensures consistent and reliable installation, thereby enhancing the overall integrity of the railway infrastructure.

Given the increasing demands on our railway networks and the necessity to maintain and expand underground lines, I firmly believe that this innovation will prove invaluable to railway maintenance crews, greatly reducing labour costs and enhancing productivity.

I hereby submit this proposal for the consideration of the Ministry, with the hope that my invention may be adopted as an official tool for railway construction and maintenance. Should further demonstrations or detailed explanations be required, I am more than willing to provide them.

Algernon Thistleton

我自己一个人走了出去。什么东西也没抢到，什么伙伴也没活下。但我安全了。

<b>目标：</b> 从布伦达·博蒙特男爵夫人处获取一份真正的皇家委任状文件。


行动策略：

由于时间限制，我们无法调动足够的资源找人替换她。不过她也基本支持我们的目标。 

根据男爵夫人的心理评估简报，推荐采取勒索策略。男爵夫人之所以能一直留任，是因为众人对她的尊敬，而非出于政治原因。自任职后，她从未以权谋私。

她只在违法违规行为发生时动用权力贯彻法律。这一情况清楚表明她本人非常重视行为的规范性。抹黑她不仅会给任务带来灾难性的后果，更会断送抹黑者的前程。


材料：

随本档案附有一份全息光盘，内含信息对信息主体的个人生活和职业生涯会带来恶劣影响。全息光盘内存有男爵夫人与其爱人——一个泰晤士人（代号为“男仆”）——之间的长期通信记录。这份敏感材料应该足以让男爵夫人妥协并服从我们。


经历概述：

男爵夫人长期活跃在各类社交活动中，是伦敦社交场中的名人，受众人欢迎——尽管此类场合的参与人数有限。她的丈夫是著名实业家温斯顿·罗林森·沙普兰。他们已结婚17年，育有二孩。尽管二人对外表现婚姻圆满幸福，但秃鹰[1-32131]曾在路易甚见过男爵夫人对他人展露过度亲昵的态度。


担任职务：

男爵夫人目前担任宫务大臣一职，受众人敬仰。她的职责为“管理”皇家地产有限公司HRM温莎，并对所有绅士会出版期刊的编辑结果有最终表决权。


M.I.C.E简介 = M(0)|I(3)|C(9)|E(5) 推荐行动方案
强制手段:: (C)>(E)>(I)>(M)

金钱（M）：男爵夫人拥有丰厚的独立收入，并继承了大笔家族遗产，同时又有职务上的财政补助。

意识形态（I）：她对为君主服务这一信念坚定不移，除此之外并无强烈的信仰和道德立场。她认为自己从事的是一项务实的工作，且从事这项工作的人也不应得到过度的关注。我们认为她在总的方面是支持我们的愿望和目标的。

强制手段（C）：博蒙特男爵夫人将自己的一生奉献给了工作。她的职业既无法损害她的公众形象，也不允许她的公众形象受损。

自我意识（E）：尽管她确有自恋的倾向，但很难以物质手段改变她的立场。因而我们什么也无法给予她，采取物质手段只会危害我们因她所拥有的权力。

divers of which Countries, and many of the Islands, Cities and Ports thereof, have long since been discovered by others of our Subjects, albeit not frequented in Trade of Merchandize. KNOW YE THEREFORE, that we, greatly tendering the Honour of our Nation, the Wealth of our People, and the Encouragement of them, and others of our loving Subjects in their good Enterprizes, for the Increase of our Navigation, and the Advancement of lawful Traffick, to the Benefit of our Common Wealth, have of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge, and mere Motion, given and granted, and by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, do give and grant unto our said loving Subjects, before in these Presents expressly named, that they and every of them from henceforth be, and shall be one Body Corporate and Politick, in Deed and in Name, by the Name of The Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and them by the Name of The Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, one Body Corporate and Politick, in Deed and in Name, really and fully, for us, our Heirs and Successors, we do order, make, ordain, constitute, establish and declare, by these Presents, and that by the same Name of Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, they shall have Succession, and that they and their Successors, by the Name of The Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, be and shall be, at all Times hereafter, Persons able and capable in Law, and a Body Corporate and Politick, and capable in Law to have, purchase, receive, possess, enjoy and retain, Lands, Rents, Priviledges, Liberties, Jurisdictions, Franchises and Hereditaments of whatsoever Kind, Nature, and Quality so ever they be, to them and their Successors. And also to give, grant, demise, alien, Assign and dispose Lands, Tenements and Hereditaments, and to do and execute all and singular other Things, by the same Name that to them shall or may appertain to do. And that they and their Successors, by the Name of The Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, may plead and be impleaded, answer and be answered, defend and be defended, in whatsoever Courts and Places, and before whatsoever Judges and Justices, and other Persons and Officers, in all and singular Actions, Pleas, Suits, Quarrels, Causes and Demands whatsoever, of whatsoever Kind, Nature or Sort, in such Manner and Form, as any other, our liege People of this our Realm of England, being Persons able and capable in Law, may or can have, purchase, receive, possess, enjoy, retain, give, grant, demise, alien, assign, dis- pose, plead and be impleaded, answer and be answered, defend and be defended, release and be released, do permit and execute. And that The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors, may have a Common Seal, to serve for all the Causes and Business of them and their Successors. And that it shall and may be lawful to The said Governor and Company, and their Successors, the same Seal, from Time to Time, at their Will and Pleasure, to break, change, and to make new or alter, as to them shall seem expedient. And further, we will, and by these presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, we do ordain, that there shall be from henceforth one of the same Company to be elected and appointed, m such Form, as hereafter in these Presents is expressed, which shall be called The Governor of the said Company, and that there shall be from henceforth Twenty- Four of the said. Company, to be elected and appointed in such Form, as hereafter in these presents is expressed, which shall be called The Committees of the said Company, who, together with the Governor of the said Company for the Time being, shall have the direction of the Voyages, of or for the said Company, and the Provision of the Shipping and Merchandizes thereto belonging, and also the sale of all Merchandizes returned in the Voyages, of or for the said Company, and the manag- ing and handling of all other Things belonging to the said com- pany and for the better Execution of this our Will and Grant in this Behalf We have assigned, nominated, constituted and made, and by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Succes- sors, we do assign, nominate, constitute and make, the said Thomas Smith, Alderman of London, to be the First and present Governor of the said Company, to continue in the said Office, from the Date of these presents, until another of the said Company shall in due Manner be chosen and sworn unto the said Office, according to the Ordinances and Provisions hereafter in these Presents expressed and declared, if the said Thomas Smith shall so long live ; and also we have assigned, nominated and appointed, and by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, we do assign, nominate, constitute and make, the said Paul Banning, Leo- nard Hollyday, John Moore, Edward Holmeden, Richard Staper, Thomas Cordell, William Garway, Oliver Style, James Lan- caster, Richard Wiseman, Francis C herry, Thomas Allabaster, William Romney, Roger How, William Chambers, Robert San- dye, John Eldred, Richard Wiche, John Hylord, John Middleton, John Comb, William Harrison, Nicholas Ling and Robert Bell, to be the Twenty-Four First and Present Committees of the said Company, to continue in the said office of Committees of the said company from the Date of these Presents, for One whole year next following. And further we will and grant, by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors, that it shall and may be lawful to and for The said Governor and Company, for the Time being, or the more part of them, present at any publick Assembly, commonly called the Court, holden for the said Company, the Governor of the said Company being always one, from Time to Time, to elect, nominate and appoint one of the said Company, to be Deputy to the said Governor, which Deputy shall take a Corporal Oath, before the Governor and Five or more of the Committees of the said Company for the Time being, well, faithfully and truly to execute his said Office of Deputy to the Governor of the said Company, and after his oath, so taken, shall and may from Time to Time, in the Absence of the said Governor, exercise and execute the Office of Governor of the said company, in such Sort as the said Governor ought to do : And further we will and grant, by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, unto the said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trad- ing into the East-Indies, and their Successors, that they or the greater Part of them, whereof the Governor for the Time being or his Deputy to be one, from Time to Time, and at all Times hereafter shall and may have Authority and Power, yearly and every year, on the First Day of July, or at any Time within Six Days after that Day, to assemble and meet toge- there, in some convenient Place, to be appointed or Deputy of the said Governor, and the said Company for the Time being or the greater Part of them, which then shall happen to be present, whereof the Governor of the said Company or his Deputy for held from the said Company, shall be in reasonable Manner set down and devised, before they shall be allowed, or admitted to trade or traffick, as a Freeman of the said Company. And further we will and grant, by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and successors, unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors, that the sa id Gover- nor, or the Deputy of the said Governor, and the Company and their Successors, for the Time being, or the greater Part of them, whereof the Governor, or the Deputy of the Governor, from Time to Time, to be one, shall and may, from Time to Tims, and at all Times hereafter, have Autho- rity and Power, yearly and every Year, on the first Day of July, or at any time within Six Diys after that Day, to assemble and meet together, in some convenient place, to be from Time to Time appointed, by the said Governor of the said Company, or in his Absence, by his Deputy : And that they being so assembled, it shall and may be law- ful, to and for the said Governor or his Deputy, and the Com- pany for the Time being, or the greater Part of them, which then shall happen to be present, whereof the Governor of the said Company, or his Deputy for the Time being, to be one, to elect and nominate Twent y-f our of the said Company, which shall be Committee of the said Company, for Ones whole Year, from thence next ensuing- which Person beinor so elected and nominated to be Committees of the said Com- pany, as aforesaid, before they be admitted to the Execution of their said Offices, shall take a Corporal Oath, before the Governor or his Deputy, and any Six or more of the said Committees of the said Company, being their last Predeces- sors for the Time being, that they and every of them shall well and faithfully perform their said O ffice of Committees, in all things concerning the same, and that immediately after the said Oath so taken, they shall and may execute and use their said Offices of Committees of the said Company, for One whole Year, from thence next followingf; and more over our Will and Pleasure is, and by these Presents, for us our Heirs and Successors, we do grant unto The said Gover- nor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and to their Successors, that when and as often as shall happen, the Governor of the said Company for the Time being, at any Time within One Year, after that he shall be nominated, elected and sworn to the office of Governor of the said Company, as is aforesaid, to die or to be removed from the said Office, which Governor, not demeaning himself well in his said Office, we will to beremoveable at the Pleasure of the said Company, or the greater Part of them, which shall be present, at any of their publick Assemblies, commonly called their General Court, holden for the said Company, that then and so often it shall and may be lawful, to and for the Residue of the said Company for the Time being, or the greater Part of them, within convenient Time after the Death or removing of any such Governor, to assemble themselves in such convenient Place as they shall think fit, for the Elec- tion of the Governor of the said Company : and that the said Company, or the greater Part of them, being then and there present, shall and may, then and there, before their Departure from the said Place, elect and nominate one other of the said Company, to be Governor of the same Company, in the Place or Stead of him that so died or was so removed, which Person, being so elected, and nominated to the Office of Governor of the said Company, shall have and exercise the said Office for and during the Residue of the said Year, taking first a Corporal Oath as is aforesaid, for the due Execution thereof ; and this to be done from Time to Time, so often as the Case shall so require. and The said Governor and Company, or the greater Part of them, whereof the Governor for the Time being, his Deputy, to be one, being then and there present, shall and may then and there, before their Departure from the said Place elect and nominate one or more of the said Company, to be Committees of the same Ccmpany, in the Places and Steads Place or Stead, of him or them . that so died, or were or was so removed, which Person or Persons, so elected and nominated to the Office or Oflfices of Committee, or Committees, of the said Company, shall have and exercise the said Office and Offices, during the Residue of the said Year, taking first a Corporal Oath as is aforesaid, for the due Execution thereof, and this to be done from Time to Time, so often as the Case shall require. And further we do, by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, will and grant unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors, that they, and all that are or shall be of The said Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and every of them, and all the Sons of them, at their several Ages of One and Twenty Years or upwards : And further, all such the Ap- prentices, Factors or Servants of them, and of every of them, which hereafter shall be employed by The said Governor and Company, in the said Trade of Merchandize, of or to the East-Indies, beyond the Seas, or any other the Places afore- said, in any part of the said East-Indies, or other the Places aforesaid, shall and may, by the Space of Fifteen Years, from the Feast of the Birth of our Lord God last past, before the Date hereof, freely traflfick and use the Trade of Merchandize, by Seas, in and by such Ways and Passages already found out and discovered, or which hereafter shall be found out and discovered, as they shall esteem and take to be fittest, into and from the said East-Indies, in the Countries and Parts of Asia and Africa, and into and from all the Islands, Ports, Havens ; Cities, Creeks, Towns and Places cf Asia and Africa, and America, or any of them, beyond the Cape of Bona Esperanza to the Straights of Magellan, where any Trade or Traffick of Merchandize may be used or had, and to and from every of them, in such Order, Manner, Form, Liberty and Condition, to all Intents and Purposes, as shall be, from Time to Time, at any publick Assembly or Court, held by or for The said Governor and Company, by or between them of the said Fellowship or Company of Merchants of London, Trad- ing into the East-Indies, or the more Part of them, for the Time being, present at such Assembly or Court, the Governor, or his Deputy, being always present at such Court or Assembly, limited and agreed, and not otherwise, without any Molesta- tion, Impeachment, or Disturbance, any Statute, Usage, Diver- sity of Religion or Faith or any other Cause or Matter what- soever, to the contrary notwithstanding : So always the same Trade be not undertaken nor addressed to any Country, Island, Port, Haven, City, Creek, Town or Place, already in the law- ful and actual Possession of any such Christian Prince or State, as at this present is, or at any Time hereafter shall be in League or Amity with us, our Heirs or Successors, and who doth not or will not accept of such Trade, but doth overtly declared and publish the same to be utterly against his or their Good Will and Liking. And further our Will and Pleasure is, and by these Presents, for us our Heirs and Successors, we do grant unto The said Governor and Company of Merch- ants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and to their Successors, that it shall and may be lawful, to and for The said Governor and Company, and their Successors, from Time to Time to assemble themselves^ for or about any the Matters, Causes, Affairs or Businesses of the said Trade, in any Place or Places, for the same convenient, during the said Term of Fif- teen Years, within our Dominions or elsewhere, and there to hold Court for the said Company, and the Affairs thereof; and that also it shall and may be lawful, to and for them, or the more Part of them, being so assembled, and that shall then and there be present, in any such Place or Places, whereof the Governor or his Deputy for the Time being, to be one, to make, ordain, and constitute such, and so many reasonable Laws, Constitutions, Orders and Ordinances, as to them, or the greater Part of them, being then and there present, shall seem necessary and convenient, for the good Government of the same Company, and of all Factors, Masters, Mariners and other Officers, employed or to be employed in any of their Voyages, and for the better Advancement and Continuance of the said Trade and Traffick, and the same Laws, Constitu- tions, Orders and Ordinances, so made, to put in use and execute accordingly, and at their Pleasure to revoke or alter the same, or any of them as Octatian shall require; and that The said Governor and Company, so often as they shall make, ordain or establish any such Laws, Constitutions, Orders or Ordinances, in Form aforesaid, shall and may lawfully impose, ordain, limit and provide such Pains, Punishments and Penal- ties, by Imprisonment of Body, or by Fines and Amerciaments, or by all or any of them upon and against all Offenders, contrary to such Laws, Constitutions, Orders and Ordinances, or any of them as to The said Governor and Company for the Time being, or the greater Part of them, then and there being present, the said Governor, or his Deputy, being always one, shall seem necessary, requisite and convenient, for the Observation of the same Laws, Constitutions, Orders and Ordinances; and the same Fine and Amerciaments shall and may levy, take and have, to the Use of The said Governor and Company, and their Successors, without the Impediment of us, our Heirs or Successors, or of any the Officers or Ministers of us, our Heirs or Successors, and without any Account thereof, to us, our Heirs or Successors, to be rendered or made ; all and singular which Laws, Constitutions, Orders and Ordinances, so as aforesaid to be made, we will to be duly observed and kept, under the Pain and Penalties therein to be contained ; so always as the said Laws, Orders, Constitutions, Ordinances, Imprisonments, Fines and Amerciaments be reasonable, and not contrary or repugnant to the Laws, Statutes, or Customs of this our Realm. And for as much as The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East- Indies, have not yet experienced of the Kinds of Commodities and Merchandizes, which are or will be vendible, or to be uttered in the said Parts of the East-Indies, and therefore shall be driven to carry to those Parts, in their Voyages outward, divers and sundry Commodities, which are likely to be return- ed again to this our Realm: We therefore of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, for the better encouraging of The said Governor and Company of Mer- chants of London, Trading into the said East Indies, and for the Advancement of the said Trade, do grant unto The said Governor and Company, and to their Successors, that they and their Successors, during the Four First Voyages, which they shall make, or set forth, for or towards the said East- Indies, shall and may transport, and carry out of our Realm of England, and the Ports, Creeks and Havens thereof, all such and so much Goods and Merchandizes, being Goods and Merchandizes lawfully passable and transportable out of this Realm, and not prohibited to be transported by any Law or Statute of this Realm, as shall be by them, their Factors Assigns, shipped in any Ship or Ships, Vessel or Vessels, to be employed in any of the said Four First Voyages, free of Custom, Subsidy or Poundage, or any other Duties or Pay- ments, to us or our Successors, due or belonging, for the shipping or transporting of the same, or any of them; and yet nevertheless our Will and Pleasure is and we do, by these Presents, straitly charge and command, that all and every such Goods and Merchandizes, so to be transport- ed out of this realm, from Time to Time, during the said Four First Voyages, as is aforesaid, shall, from Time to Time, be duly entered by the Customer, Controller or other Officer of such Port, Creek or Place, where the same Goods and Merchandizes shall happen to be ship- ped and loaden, before such Time as the same shall be shipped, or loaden, to be transported as is aforesaid : And also of our further especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, we do, for us, our Heirs and Succes- sors, grant to and with the said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East Indies, and their successors, that when and as often, at any Time, during the said Time and space of Fifteen years, as any custom. Poundage, Subsidy, or other duties, shall be due and payable unto us, our Heirs, or Successors, for any goods, Wares, or Merchandizes whatsoever, to be returned out or from any the Islands, Ports, Havens, Cities, Towns or places aforesaid, unto our Port of London, or any of the Havens, Creeks, Members or Places to the same Port belonging, that the customers and all other Officers for the Time being, of us, our Heirs or Suc- cessors, for or concerning Receipts of Customs, Poundage, Subsidies or other Duties, unto whom it shall appertain, shall upon the Request of the Governor and Company of the said Merchants of London, Trading into the East Indies, or any their Agents, Factors or Assigns, give unto the said Gover- nor and Company, their Agents, Factors or Assigns, Six Months' time, for payment of the one Half, and after those Six months ended, other Six Months' Time, for the payment of the other Half, of their said customs, Poundage, or other subsidy or duties, receiving good ]and sufficient bonds, with Surety, to the Use of us, our Heirs and Successors, for the true payment of the same accordingly ; and Power, in Form aforesaid, to trade and traffick to and from the said East-Indies, and all and every the Parts thereof, in Form aforesaid, according to the Orders, Ordinances and Agreements hereafter to be made and agreed upon, by The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trad- ing into the East-Indies, and their Successors, or the more Part of them, present at any Court or Ships, sailing into the said East Indies, must take their due and proper Times, to proceed in their Voyages, which otherwise, as we well perceive, cannot be performed in the Rest of the Year following: Therefore we of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, for us, our Heirs and Successors, do grant, to and with The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors, that, in any Time of Restraint, Six good Ships and Six good Pinnaces, well furnished with Ordnance, and other Munition for their Defence, and Five Hundred Mariners, English Men, to guide and sail in the same Six Ships and Six Pinnaces, at all Times, during the said Term of Fifteen Years, shall quietly be permitted and suffered to depart, and go in the said Voyages, according to the purport of these presents, without any Stay or Contradiction, by us, our Heirs or Successors, or by the Lord High Admiral, or any other Officer or Subject of us, our Heirs or Successors, for the Time being, in any wise, any Restraint, Law, Statute, Usage or Matter whatsoever, to the contrary notwithstanding. Provided nevertheless, that if we shall, at any Time within the said Term of Fifteen Years, have just Cause to arm our Navy in Warlike Manner, in Defence of our Realm, or for Offence of our Enemies, or that it shall be found needful to join to the Navy of us, our Heirs or Successors, the Ships of our Subjects, to be also armed for the Wars, to such a Number as cannot be supplied, if the said Six Ships and Six Pinnaces should be permitted to depart, as above is mentioned, then upon Knowledge given, by us, our Heirs or Successors, or by our Admiral to The said Governor and Company, about the 20th Day of the Month of July, or Three Months before The said Governor and Company shall begin to make ready the same Six Ships and Six Pinnaces, that we may not spare the said Six Ships and Six Pinnaces, and the Mariners requisite for them, to be out of our Realm during the Time that our Navy shall be upon the Seas, that then the said Governor and Company shall forbear to send Six such Ships and Six Pinnaces, for their Trade and Merch- andize, until that we shall revoke or withdraw our said Navy from the said Service : and we of our further Royal Favour, and of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motions have granted, and by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, do grant to The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East- Indies, and to their Successors that the said East-Indies, nor the Islands, Havens, Ports, Cities, Towns or Places thereof nor any part thereof shall not be visited, frequented or haunted by any of the Subjects of us, our Heirs or Successors, during the same Term of Fifteen Years, contrary to the true Meaning of these Presents : And by Virtue of our Prerogative Royal, which we will not in that behalf have argued, or brought in Question we straitly charge, command and prohibit, for us, our Heirs and Successors, all the Subjects of us, our Heirs and Successors, of what Degree or Quality soever they be, that none of them, directly or indirectly do visit, haunt, frequent or trade, traffick or adventure, by way of merchandise into or from any of the said East-Indies, or into or from any the Islands, Ports, Havens, Cities, Towns or Places aforesaid, other than the said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and such particular Persons as now be, or hereafter shall be of that Company, their Agents, Factors and Assigns during the said Term of Fifteen Years, unless it be by and with such License and Agreement of the said Gover- nor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, in writing first had and obtained, under their Common Seal to be granted, upon Pain that every such Per- son or Persons that shall trade or traffick into or from any of the said East-Indies, other than the said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East- Indies, and their Successors, shall incur our Indignation, and the Forfeiture and Loss of the Goods, Merchandizes, and other Things whatever, which so shall be brought into this Realm of England, or any the Dominions of the same, con- trary to our said Prohibition, or the Purport or true Meaning of these Presents, as also the Ship and Ships with the Fur- niture thereof, wherein such Goods, Merchandizes, or Things shall be brought; the One Half of all the said Forfeitures to be to us, our Heirs and Successors, and the other Half of all and every the said Forfeitures, we do, by these Presents, of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, clearly and wholly for us, our Heirs and Successors, give, and grant unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies : And further all and every the said Offenders, for their said Contempt, to suffer Imprisonment during our Pleasure, and such other Punishment, as to us, our Heirs or Successors, for so high a Contempt, shall seem meet and convenient, and not to be in anywise delivered, until they and every of them shall become bound unto the said Governor for the Time being in the sum of £1,ooo at the least, at no Time then after, during this Present Grant, to sail or traffick into any of the said East- Indies, contrary to our express Commandment in that Behalf herein set down and published: And further, for the better Encouragement of Merchants,' Strangers or others, to bring in Commodities into our Realm, we for us, our Heirs and Successors, do grant unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, that they and their Successors, may, from Time to Time, for any Consideration or Benefit, to be taken to their own Use, grant or give License, to any the Person or Persons to sail, trade or Traffic into or from any the said East-Indies, so as such Li- cense be granted or given, before such Goods. Wares and Merchandizes be laid on Land, and so as such License be made by the said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, for the Time being, under their Common Seal : And further of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, we have condescended and granted, and by these Presents, for us, our Heirs and Successors, we do condescend and grant unto The said Governor and Company of merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors that we, our Heirs and Successors, during the said Term of fifteen Years, will not grant Liberty, License or Power to any Person or Persons whatsoever, contrary to the Tenor of these our Letters Patents, to sail, pass, trade or traffick, to the said East-Indies, or into or from the Islands, Ports, Havens, Cities, Towns or Places aforesaid, or any of them, contrary to the true Meaning of these Presents, without the Consent of The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, or the most Part of them : And our Will and Pleasure is, and hereby we do also ordain, that it shall and may be lawful, to and for The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, or the more Part of them, whereof the Gov- ernor for the Time being, or his Deputy, to be one, to admit into and to be of the said Company, all such Apprentices, to any of The said Fellowship or Company, and all such Servants and Factors, of and for the said Company, and all such other, as to them, or the most Part of them, present at any Court, held for- the said Company, the Governor, or his Deputy, being one, shall be thought fit and agreeable, with the Orders and Ordinances to be made for the Government of the said Company. Provided always, that if any of the Persons, before named and appointed, by these Presents, to be free of The said Company of Merchants of London, Trad- ing into the East-Indies, shall not before the going forth of the Fleet, appointed for this First Voyage, from the port of London, bring in and deliver to the Treasurer or Treasurers appointed, or which, within the Space of Twenty Days next after the Date hereof, shall be appointed, by the said Gover- nor and Company, or the more Part of them, to receive the Contributions and Adventures, set down by the several Ad- venturers, in this last and present Voyage, now in hand, to be set forth, such Sums of Money as have been, by any of the said Persons, by these presents, nominated to be of the said Company, expressed, set down and written in a Book for that Purpose, and left in the Hands of the said Thomas Smith, Governor of the said Company, or of the said Paul Banning, Alderman of London, and subscribed with the Names of the same Adventurers, under their Hands, and agreed upon to be adventured in the said First Voyage, that then, it shall be lawful for The said Governor and Company, or the more Part of them, whereof the said Governor or his Deputy, to be one, at any their General Court, or General Assembly, to remove, disfranchise and displace him or them at their Wills and Pleasures. And the said Governor and Company, of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, for them and their Successors, do, by these Presents, covenant, promise and grant, to and with us, our Heirs and Successors, that they The said Governor and Company, and their Suc- cessors, in all and every such Voyages, as they at any Time or Times hereafter, during the said Term, shall make out of this Realm, by Virtue of this our Grant and Letters Patents, the First Voyage only excepted, shall and will, upon every Return which shall be made back again into this Realm, or any of our Dominions, or within Six Months next after every such Return, bring into this our Realm of England, from the said East-Indies, or from some other Parts, beyond the Seas, out of our Dominions as great or greater Value in Bullion of Gold or Silver, or other foreign Coin of Gold or Silver, respectively, for every Voyage, the First Voyage only excepted, as shall be by Force of these Presents trans- ported and carried out of this Realm, by them or any of them, in any Kind of Silver abovesaid whatsoever, in any of the said Voyages ; and that all such Silver, as by Virtue of this our Grant and Letters Patents, shall be shipped or laden by The said Governor and Company, or their Successors, to be transported out of this Realm, in any of the said Voyages, shall from Time to Time, at the setting forth of every such particular Voyage, be shipped and laden at the Ports or Havens of London, Dartmouth, or Plymouth, or at some of the same Ports or Havens, and at no other Port or Haven whatsoever, within this our Realm, or the Dominions thereof ; and that all and every such Silver, as from Time to Time shall be shipped and loaden in the said Ports of London, Dartmouth, or Plymouth, or any of them, to be by Force of these Presents transported out of this Realm, as is aforesaid shall from Time to Time be duly entered by the Customer, Controller, Collector or other Officer to whom it shall appertain, of every such Port or Haven, where the same shall happen to be shipped or laden, in the Custom-Book belonging to the said Port or Haven, before such Time as the same shall be shipped or laden, to be transported as is aforesaid, without any Custom or Subsidy, to be paid for the same ; and that in like Manner,'all and all Manner of Gold and Silver whatso- ever which shall be brought into this Realm, or any of our Dominions, by The said Governor and Company, or any of them, according to the true Meaning of these Presents, shall likewise be, from Time to Time, duly entered by the Customer, Controller, or other Officer of every such Port, Creek or Place, where the same Gold or Silver shall happen to be unshipped, or brought to Land, before such Time as the same Gold or Silver or any Part thereof, shall be unshipped or brought to Land, as is aforesaid. Provided always, nevertheless, and our Will and Pleasure is, that these our Letters Patents, or any Thing therein contained, shall not in any Sort extend to give or grant any License, Power or Authority unto The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, or to any of them to undertake or address any Trade unto any Country, Port, Island, Haven, City, Creek, Town or Place, being already in the lawful and actual Possession of any such Christian Prince or State, as at this present is, or at any Time hereafter shall be in League or Amity, with us, our Heirs or Successors, and which doth not, or will not accept of such Trade, but doth overtly declare and publish the same, to be utterly against his or their Good-Will and Liking, any Thing before in these presents contained, to the contrary thereof notwith- standing. Provided also, that if it shall, hereafter appear to us, our Heirs or Successors, that this Grant or the Con- tinuance thereof, in the Whole or in any Part thereof, shall not be profitable to us, our Heirs and Successors, or to this our Realm, that then,' and from thenceforth, upon and after Two Years Warning, to be given to the said Company, by us, our Heirs or Successors, under our or their Privy Seal, or Sign Manual, this present Grant shall cease, be void and determined, to all Intents, Constructions and Purposes : And further of our especial Grace, certain Knowledge and mere Motion, we have condescended and granted, and by these Presents for us our Heirs and Successors, do condescend and grant to The said Governor and Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, and their Successors that if at the End of the said Term of Fifteen Years, it shall seem meet and Convenient unto The said Governor and Com- pany, or any the Parties aforesaid, that this present Grant shall be continued, and if that also it shall appear unto us, our Heirs and Successors, that the Continuance thereof shall not be prejudicial or hurtful to this our Realm, but that we shall find the further Continuance thereof profitable for us, our Heirs and Successors, and for our Realm, with such Condi- tions as are herein mentioned, or with some Alteration or Qualification thereof, that then we, our Heirs or Successors, at the Instance and humble Petition of The said Governor and Company, or any of them, to be made unto us, our Heirs and Successors, will grant and make unto The said Governor and Company, or any of them, so suing for the same ; and such other Person and Persons, our Subjects, as they shall nomi- nate and appoint, or shall be by us, our Heirs or Successors, newly nominated, not exceeding in Number Twenty-Four, new Letters Patents, under the Great Seal of England, in due Form of Law, with the like Covenants, Grants, Clauses and Articles, as in these Presents are contained, or with Addition of other necessary Articles, or changing of these into some other Parts, for and during the full Term of Fifteen Years, then next following ; willing hereby and straitly charging and commanding all and singular our Admirals, Vice-Admirals Justices, Mayors, Sheriffs, Escheators, Constables, Bailiffs, and all and singular other our Officers, Ministers, Liege Men and Subjects whatsoever, to be aiding, favouring helping and assisting unto The said Governor and Company, and to their Successors, and to their Deputies, Officers, Factors, Servants Assigns and Ministers and every of them, in executing and enjoying the Premises, as well on Land as on Sea, from Time to Time, when you or any of you shall thereunto be required, any Statue, Act, Ordinance, Proviso, Proclamation or Re- straint, heretofore had, made, set forth, ordained, or provided, or any other Matter, Cause or Thing whatsoever, to the contrary in any way notwithstanding ; although express Mention of the true yearly Value or Certainty of the Premises, or of any of them, or of any other Gifts or Grants, by us, or any of our Progenitors, to the said Governor and. Company of Merchants of London, Trading into the East-Indies, or to any of them, before this Time made, in these Presents is not made, or any Statute, Act, Ordinance, Provision Proclamation or Restraint, to the contrary heretofore had made, ordained or provided, or any other Thing, Cause or Matter whatsoever, in any wise notwithstanding. In Witness whereof, we have caused these our Letters to be made Patents : Witness Ourself, at Westminster, the Thirty-first Day of December, in the Three and Fortieth Year of our Reign.

5. After the steeping time is up, strain the nettle tea into your teacup.

This might be my last entry. I fell from a high place and I think my back is broken. I'm in so much pain and I can't move. I'm writing this in the hope that someone will find it and give it to my mother. She's in a wheelchair and runs a small roadside shop along the racetrack in Hackney. Please tell her I love her and that I'm sorry for breaking my promise.
</font>'''
'''<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
记录1：
妈妈要我保证用这本日志记录我在哈克尼外的旅行。不知道这对她有什么好处，还是说能让我妹妹了解外面的世界，哪怕最后也只是让妈妈用这些字来来吓唬她，让她留在家里。离开圆徽帮安全的领地，这事想想都怪，但我也等不及要看看外面的世界。我在今天走出了我们的领地，看到了远处城市的天际线——真壮观啊。

记录2：
我在一栋老旧的废弃建筑里找到了一罐豆子。虽然不多，但聊胜于无。我还看到了一群流浪狗。它们看着很狂躁，我只能靠断掉的扫帚柄打跑它们。希望之后不会再碰上它们。

记录3：
我偶遇了一伙正在收集补给的求生者。他们很友好，还分了点水给我。他们告诉我附近有栋防御良好的建筑，里面有求生者社区。我明天说不定会去看看。

记录4：
我找到了卷强力胶！虽然看上去没什么，但在这里它是宝贵的资源。它可以用来修理坏掉的装备，或者临时修补建筑结构。我感觉自己捡到宝了。

最后的记录：
这大概是我最后的记录了。我从高处摔了下来，背应该摔断了。好痛，动都不能动。希望有人能找到我写下的东西然后交给我的妈妈。她是个坐轮椅的女人，在哈克尼的跑道旁开着一家小店。请告诉她我爱她，我很抱歉没能遵守诺言。

'''<font face='$BRODY'> 
Day 1: Today is the day I set out beyond the borders of Westminster, as my mother has requested. I am both nervous and excited to see what lies beyond our gated territory. I packed light and brought a few tins of food to sustain me on my journey. I hope to come across some new sights and meet interesting people.

Day 3: So far, my journey has been uneventful. I decided to not hang around the riff raff in the slums and thus walked for miles just to try and find some civilisation.

Day 4: I came across an abandoned building where I found some duct tape and used it to fix a hole in my shoe which I managed to gain by stepping on broken glass. People really don't tidy up out here like they do back in Westminster, utter savages. I also encountered some stray cats that seemed to have mange. I had to fight them off with a bunch of rocks to keep them from attacking me. I've never seen anything so scary!

Day 5: I found a small village today and stopped to rest. The people there were friendly and offered me a place to sleep for the night. they found everything I said very amusing, as if I was some type of comedian. I also learned that there is a war brewing outside of Westminster... something to do with Knights and Columns?. This news was disheartening, but I am determined to keep going.

Day 7: I have seen things I never thought I would see. The world beyond Westminster is harsh and unforgiving. I witnessed a group of soldiers commit unspeakable acts against innocent people. I fear for my safety and the safety of my family. I must return to Westminster and warn them of the danger that lies beyond our borders.

Day 19: I apologies for failing to write more often as I had wished, trying to survive out there is far more important than writing a journal! I am beginning to realise how unequipped and how naive I was to come out here.

Day 20: I know that my time is limited and that I will not make it back to Westminster. I hope that someone finds this journal and knows the difficulties I went though. I just wish my mother know what she sent me out into... Maybe she did?

Dear reader, I hope you can find a way to survive in this cruel world. As for me, I accept my fate and am at peace with it. Goodbye.

- Clifford Curry II
</font>'''
'''<font face='$BRODY'> 
第一天：今天是我按照妈妈的要求离开威斯敏斯特的日子。我既紧张，又很激动，想看看大门外的世界。我带的行李不多，只有几个在路上充饥的罐头。希望能发现些新东西，见到些有趣的人。

第三天：到目前为止，我的旅途还是很单调。我决定离开低贱的贫民窟，我要走上几英里的路去找到别的人烟。

第四天：我在一栋废弃的建筑里找到了些强力胶，用它们补上了鞋子因为踩上碎玻璃弄出的洞。这里不像威斯敏斯特，当地人一点也不讲卫生，完全就是野人。我还碰到了些似乎患了兽疥癣的流浪猫。为了防止它们攻击，我只能拿石头赶跑它们。从没见过这么吓人的东西！

第五天：今天找到了个小村庄并在那落脚休息。那里的人很友好，给了我一个过夜的地方。不论我说什么他们都觉得有趣，好像我是什么喜剧演员似的。我还了解到威斯敏斯特外有一场战争正在酝酿……好像是和什么骑士还有纵队有关？虽然这个消息不免让人有些沮丧，但我还是要继续走下去。

第七天：我已经见过了很多我想都没想过的事情。威斯敏斯特外的世界严酷又残忍。我目睹过一群士兵对无辜老百姓犯下语言都形容不了的罪行。我为自己的安全和家人的安全感到无比担心。我必需回到威斯敏斯特，告诉他们外面的危险。

第十九天：抱歉隔了那么久。尽管我很想写，但在外面求生远比写日记要重要！我开始意识到自己来这里时装备带得多么不足，自己当时也多么天真。

第二十天：我知道自己大限将至，也清楚自己没法回到威斯敏斯特了。希望有人能找到这本日记，了解我经历过的磨难。我只愿妈妈知道把我派到了个什么样的地方……也许她知道呢？

亲爱的读者，我希望你能在这个残酷的世界活下去。至于我，我接受命运的安排，毫无怨言。再会。

-克利福德·柯里二世
</font>'''

<p align='center'>
<u>迷人花园小矮人：</u>

Oi Bert,

Well, here we are, mate. It's been a right ol' mess, innit? Can't say we didn't try, but I'm proper knackered now, so I reckon it's time I cancel me subscription to this thing we call life. Not like I'm gettin' me money's worth, anyway.

Cheers, Louis
</font>'''
'''<font face='$HandwrittenFont'> 
喂，博尔特：

咱们的事就这样了，伙计。真是一团糟啊，你说呢？咱们肯定试过了，但我现在真没力气了，所以这次我打算不再跟着这个叫生活的东西走了。总之我大概也弄不到什么值钱的玩意儿。

伦敦本该是最后一站，但它不是。我希求的快乐它没有给我。不知道我以前怎么从来都没想过……或者其实我想过。我不是在找什么东西或者什么地方，而是在找一个人，而且她不是别人。她一直都在这里，她就是我想要的全部，但她却不想和我有任何交集。
她就是我曾拥有的一切，如今却从我的生命中离去。可能我对她来说从来就什么都不是吧。
这样最好。
这么久以来，早该这么做了。我终于找到了可以结束痛苦的方法。

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <3>
'''Everyone... the neighbours, the kids, the Hackney Gazette! "Mole Man of Hackney", they call me. Think it's clever. Cute. Like it's a hobby.

They don't know the truth. This house was built on Roman land. I've seen the maps. Old gold routes. There was a mine here before the Victorians bricked it over and called it civilised. I haven't just been digging tunnels. I've been excavating history. They mock what they don't understand.'''
'''每个人……邻居、小孩，还有《哈克尼报》！“哈克尼的鼹鼠人”，他们就是这么叫我的。还以为这名字取得挺聪明，觉着挺可爱，就像是在说谁的爱好似的。

他们不知道实情。这座房子其实建在罗马人的土地上。我已经看过地图了。这里在以前的淘金路线上，曾有座矿井，直到被维多利亚时期的人用砖头堵上，管这叫“文明之举”。我一直在挖隧道。我已经查遍了史书。他们这是在嘲笑自己不理解的东西。'''

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <4>
All roads lead to Rome!
条条大路通罗马！

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <5>
'''Tunnel depth is getting around 14.6 metres-ish? The bloody humidity though, it's as thick as soup. And oh boy, the pressure is rising! BUT! Last night I hit stonework - old brick, not London brick. Roman, maybe.

Coin under it. Real gold. Worn edges. Laurel wreath. Emperor's face scratched off. They did that when they lost faith in them, didn't they? Damnatio memoriae.
I'm close now. The gold's talking. Can feel it through the pickaxe. Vibrations up the bone. It's a Gold Ore vein, I know it!'''
'''隧道的深度大概到了14.6米？潮是真得潮，下去就跟在汤里似的。而且啊，压力也在增加！但是！昨晚我挖到了石质结构——是旧砖头，而且不是伦敦的砖，可能是罗马的。

下面有硬币，罗马金币。边缘磨损了。有桂冠。皇帝的脸被刮去了。他们在对皇帝失去信仰后做的，是不是？Damnatio Memoriae（记忆抹杀）。
我离得很近了，能听到金子在说话，能通过镐子感受到。骨子里都在震动。这是条金矿脉，我就知道！'''

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <6>
FOUND IT.
找到了。

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <7>
'''Gold. Solid. Heavy. Still warm from the earth. Pulled out three ores, crusted in red soil like scabs. Now it's mine. All the years, all the noise, all the names - and now I'm rich in the oldest way a man can be.

No one will believe me. But I don't need them to. This gold ore treasure is real. The tunnels are alive. I've woken it. Can't stop now!'''
'''金子。实打实的。沉甸甸的。土里出来的时候还暖着。挖出了三块矿石，裹着痂似的红土。现在是我的了。那么多年，那么多闲言，那么多外号——现在，我用了世界上最古老的办法，成了有钱人。

没人会相信我。但我不需要他们相信。这些金矿石是货真价实的宝藏。隧道是活的。我唤醒了它。现在不能停下！'''

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <8>

健康和安全。扯淡。

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_HackneyMoleHouse <9>
'''Council sent their inspectors. "Health and safety" they said. Want to move me to some tower flat??? Said I'm a risk to the public. They don't see. They'll never see.
But I'll show them.

Tomorrow morning I'll take them into the tunnel. Let them see the gold ore. The walls breathe with fucking WEALTH down there. Once you're inside, it knows you.

They'll understand and leave me to my gold ore, or they'll sleep. Deep in the clay. The earth is generous to those who serve it.'''
'''市议会派了检查员来。他们说：“健康和安全”。想把我关到什么塔里关着？？？他们说我对公众构成了风险。他们不明白。他们永远也不会明白。
但我会展示给他们看。

明天早上，我会带他们进隧道。让他们看看金矿石。下面的墙壁呼吸出的可是他妈的财富。谁进去，就都能明白。

他们会理解我的，会让我和我的金矿待一块，不然就得睡在下面。深深裹在黏土里。地球对侍奉它的人非常慷慨。'''

ENTRY #001 - 12 December, 18:42
记录#001——12月12日，18:42

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_HackneyPollock <4>
'''Found an article again on the Mole Man today. Been reading and rereading it for years. Felt different this time. Electric.

If he dug that many metres down and reached the water table... well, I reckon he went beyond. They say the Council tried filling the tunnels with aerated concrete. Rubbish. You can't plug up a tunnel like that.

I'm starting my own. The Roundel Council people won't stop me. Not this time. Not like the basement dig of last year...

Tunnel begins beneath the kitchen. Floor's already up. Bought a pickaxe from a man in Eastminster who winked when I told him what it was for.'''
'''今天又找到了篇关于鼹鼠人的文章。这几年来我读了一遍又一遍，但这次的感觉却不一样。有点激动。

要是他挖了那么深，到了地下水位……我觉得他挖得还要深。他们说市议会试过用充满二氧化碳的混凝土填满隧道。白费力气。堵住隧道怎么能用这种方法。

我开始了自己的挖掘大计。圆徽帮议会的人没法阻止我。他们这次绝对阻止不了我，去年在地下室挖洞那次的事不会再发生了……

隧道口开在厨房下。地板已经掀开。我从伊斯敏斯特的一个人那买了镐子，告诉他这是用来做什么的后，他还朝我眨了眨眼睛。'''

Captain of the Guard's Terminal
守卫队长的终端机

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <2>
Entry I - Rousing the Troops 
条目I——激发士气

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <3>
Another dawn over Camelot, and the lads were dragging their feet like irradiated commuters in full plate. I swear, if I have to shout "FORM RANKS" one more time before sun-up, I'll end up hoarse for life. Still, I put 'em through the paces. Sword drills. Marching formations. Even had 'em recite oaths of fealty to Arthur until their tongues twisted! Ha! Morale's been wavering since the situation in Eastminster though, I really thought we were beyond all that now we've got this new Camelot? A few stern words and a cold dip in the Sleipnir trough sorted that out. Camelot doesn't tolerate slackers - not while I wear the Captain's pauldron!
卡美洛又迎来了新的一天，穿戴好全身护甲的伙计们昂首阔步，就像被辐射的通勤鬼那样精神。我发誓，要是在太阳升起前得再多喊一次“集合”，那我这辈子都得沙哑着嗓子过日子了。但我还是考验了他们。刀剑训练，整队列队，甚至让他们背诵效忠亚瑟的誓言，直到舌头打结！哈！自伊斯敏斯特一事后，士气一直不稳，我真心认为虽然我们组建了新卡美洛，但也只是有了支队伍而已？说几句严厉的话，把脑袋按到八蹄马槽的冷水里一会儿，这样足够解决问题了。卡美洛不容懒鬼——至少在我还带着队长的肩甲时不容！

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <4>
Entry II - Round Table Inspection
条目II——圆桌视察

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <5>
Lancelot came back from out of town today, all polished silver and solemn eyes. The Round Table guards inspected every corner of the barracks - beds made, weapons oiled, armour gleaming. They even sniffed the ale barrels for contraband (rightly so, considering what happened last month with those defectors). I saw the glint of approval in Lancelot's eye as he passed the infirmary. "Order is strength," he said. I bowed, and he clapped me on the shoulder. I dare say we've earned a full moon's peace without another formal reprimand. Pukka.
兰斯洛特今天从城外回来了，他浑身穿着抛光的银甲，眼里满是严肃。圆桌守卫检查了营房的角角落落——床铺得怎么样，武器上油没有，护甲有没有闪闪发光。他们为了搜违禁品，甚至还闻了麦芽酒桶（倒也合理，毕竟上个月那几个叛逃者就这么干的）。兰斯洛特走过医务室时，我看到他的眼中露出了一丝赞许。“很有秩序。”他说。我鞠躬，他则拍了拍我的肩膀。我敢说我们为自己赢得了一个月的安宁，不用再被通报批评了。太好了。

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <6>
Entry III - Bolstering the Archers
条目III——加强弓箭手

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <7>
Took a party of newbies out to the range for archery drills. Half couldn't string a bow without nearly taking their own eye out. Still, there's promise. By midday, a young squire managed a bullseye - and with wind, no less. I've requisitioned fresh string from the armoury and told Percival to find us more longbow blueprints from any Museum pre-war texts. If the Column horde comes crawling over Eastminster again, they'll be greeted with a sky full of iron-feathered death. Honour in precision, that's what I say.
带了一帮新兵去射击场练习射箭。一半人不差点弄瞎自己的眼睛就没法拉开弓。但他们还有点希望。到了中午，一个年轻扈从射中了靶心——而且竟然还是在刮风的情况下。我从军火库里征用了新弓弦，让珀西瓦尔替我们去博物馆的战前文本里多找些长弓蓝图。要是纵队那帮人再度染指伊斯敏斯特，那家等着漫天的箭雨夺走他们的性命吧。精准中蕴含的荣誉，这就是我认同的。

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <8>
Entry IV - Gate Duty and the Omen
条目IV——守门职责和预兆

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_WandsworthCOTG <9>
Was on rounds near the main gate when I noticed the gate had slipped half an inch from it's rails. Not enough to spot at a glance, but just enough to let a Radshrew or worse - through. Barked orders at the Gatekeepers and stood watch myself as they sorted it out. Later, one of the squires swore he saw a cloaked figure near the outer ridge. I'm not one for superstitions, but in Camelot, every shadow could be a spy, a scavver, or a dickhead from the 5th Column. The gate is being fully fixed tonight. It must.
巡查到主门附近的时候注意到大门滑开了半英寸。一眼看过去发现不了，但是恰好足够让辐射食虫鼠或者更糟糕的东西进来。我喊来守门人，亲自看着他们解决这个问题。之后，一位扈从发誓自己看到有个带兜帽的人在外面的山嵴上。我虽然不是迷信的人，但在卡美洛，每一道阴影都可能是间谍、拾荒者，或者是来自第五纵队的蠢货。大门今晚已完全修复。必须如此。

The bigger challenge is keeping the crew out of the way in the process. Some of them don't see the point of trapping the commuters, 'might as well just kill 'em now' they say. They've got no love of the game. I found a book once - there were pictures of these huge arenas. Hundreds, maybe thousands of people turned up to watch those fights. Glorious battles - men fighting each other or even exotic beasts. Where's that passion gone? 
今天拖进来好几个。那几个狂尸鬼似乎是被我的新配方吸引了，等他们一进告解室，我就能轻松关住。更大的难点在于让其他人在办事时离远点。有些人不理解关住通勤鬼的意义，说什么“不如直接杀了他们”。他们这叫不懂打猎的乐趣。我曾找到本书，上面画着巨大的竞技场。几百号、可能几千号人坐在边上看里面打架。都是些光荣的战斗——人互相打，甚至和异域的野兽打。这样的热情到哪儿去了？

Log #1 - Ol'Blighty, Here I Come!
日志#1——英国，我来啦！

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_REMichelLichand <4>
'''O''Blighty! The land of tea, crumpets, and, as I've discovered, some of the most deranged wildlife I've ever encountered and I hail from Brazil! Now, after my stop in that diabolical place - Boston, USA - I've hunted my fair share of beasts across the world, conquered them, and then thought, "Why not pop across the pond?"

All I have from my true home is my trusty rifle. Never lets me down. Unlike British weather, which lets everyone down. Constantly. So I'm told!

First impressions of London? Grim. Everything is either grey, damp, or actively trying to steal my boots. But I am not deterred! This expedition will be my greatest yet. I shall hunt, I shall triumph, and I shall find out why everything here smells faintly of old socks.'''
'''英国！茶的故乡、松饼的王国，还有——我已经发现了——一些最疯狂的野生动物的所在之地！从巴西来的我可从没碰到过这些东西！在美国的波士顿那个糟糕透顶的地方短暂停留后，我已经找到过了全球的许多野兽，一一征服了它们。然后我忽然想到“为什么不到大西洋的另一头去？”

我真正的家乡给我剩下的，只有一把可靠的步枪。它从没让我失望——不像英国的天气，总让所有人失望，一直都这样。至少别人是这么和我说的！

对伦敦第一印象？阴冷凄凉。东西是灰色潮湿的，人是一天到晚想偷我靴子的。但这吓不倒我！这场远征将会成为我目前为止最伟大的一次。我将狩猎，我将胜利，我将知道为什么这里所有东西都闻着一股淡淡的旧袜子味。'''

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_REMichelLichand <5>
Log #2 - The Mittenlurk Incident
日志#2——巨闸蟹意外

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_REMichelLichand <6>
'''I have come to the regrettable realisation that stepping into the Thames was a mistake.

I was in pursuit of a creature they call the "Mittenlurk." It's like the American Mirelurk, except somehow more hairy. Judging by the posters it says it's originally from China... I couldn't resist my urge! But yes, Mittenlurk! Hairy, but angrier, and prone to pinching anything within reach. After a vicious battle that involved a lot of undignified splashing, I emerged victorious.

However, I now seem to be melting and turning somewhat blue? Also, my fingers are webbing slightly. I assume this is a normal part of British assimilation.'''
'''我后悔地意识到，到泰晤士河里头是个错误。

我当时正在追踪一种本地人叫“巨闸蟹”的生物。长得像美国的泥沼蟹，不过毛更多。从海报上看，它来自中国……真是激动难耐啊！是的，巨闸蟹！毛更多，脾气更大，更喜欢夹住钳子范围内的所有东西。在水中相当不得体的经历了一场恶战后，我取得了胜利。

可是，我现在似乎在融化，在变成了什么蓝色的东西？而且我的手指间也生出了点网一样的东西。大概是融入英国的正常环节吧。'''

Log #3 - I Think I'm a Thames Mutant
日志#3——我觉得自己成了泰晤士河变种人

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_REMichelLichand <8>
'''It's official. The Thames has done something to me.

My skin has taken on an unsettling sheen, I crave water more than usual, and I swear I can hold my breath longer than I could before. I'm not saying I'm mutating, but if I start developing gills, I may have to rethink my life choices.

On the bright side, I have developed an incredible ability to detect fish from a distance. A superpower, perhaps? Only time will tell.'''
'''这是真的。泰晤士河改变了我。

我的皮肤有了让人不安的光泽，我比平常更渴望到水里去，而且我发誓我屏气的时间也比以前长。不是说我没再继续变异，但要是我真长出了腮，那我就得重新考虑自己的人生选择了。

往好处想，我已经有了从远处就能发现鱼的超凡本领。说不定是种超能力？到底怎么回事，只有走一步看一步了。'''

Log #5 - My Backstory if I don't escape
日志#5——要是没能逃过一劫，提前留个生平故事

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_REMichelLichand <12>
'''Currently stuck on a tube train. A MONSTER of a Rad-Rat has me stuck on a train. So if I don't get off, here's a little about me....

I was born in Brazil, a land of beauty, jungles, and creatures that could kill you with a glance. I moved to America, land of opportunity and more creatures that could kill you with a glance. I made my home in Boston, where I hunted, collected trophies, and then realised I really really really wanted more... (Mostly because Boston sucks).

So, I packed everything I could, took Brazilian Real (My gun), and came here to Ol'Blighty. So far, I have fought mutant crabs, become partially aquatic, and nearly died at the hands of a mutant rat. That's it. End log.'''
'''我现在正被困在一列地铁里。有头辐射鼠怪物把我堵在了里面。所以要是我没能逃出去，我打算先简单介绍下自己……

我出生在巴西，一片美丽的土地，那里丛林密布，各种生物能在瞬间就杀了你。我后来移居美国，那是一片充满机遇的土地，也有更多能在瞬间就杀了你的生物。我在波士顿安了家，在那狩猎和收集各种战利品。后来我发现我真的真的真的想要更多战利品……（主要是因为波士顿太烂了。）

所以我打包了能打包的一切，带上了“真正的巴西人”（我的枪），来到了这里：英国。目前为止，我已经打败了变种螃蟹，成了半个水生动物，还差点死在一头变种老鼠的爪子里。就这样。日志结束。'''

But a British version of a Yao Guai? That would be a prize worthy of my mantle. Apparently, it's the only one in existence over here too!

Can you imagine? I can kill the only one in existence!'''
'''今天，我开始了一场新的远征——目前为止最重要的一场。要猎什么？一头传奇野兽。

美国人称之为“妖怪”，但在英国，人们管它叫……“辐射熊”。就这名。就叫“辐射熊”。听着像是他们集体放弃了动脑子一样。

总之，这场狩猎将会是我的人生巅峰。我已经有了一大堆死亡爪、泥沼蟹，以及偶尔想抢劫我的掠夺者的脑袋。但英国版的妖怪？这可配得上我的职业生涯荣耀。而且很明显，这里就这么一头！

The plan nears fruition. My Thameshounds - sleek, obedient, and bristling with potential - are nearly ready. They swim silent beneath the filth of the river, their harnesses now reinforced to bear a more... persuasive payload. Soon, the lords and lawmakers of Ol'Blighty will learn that the waters they take for granted belong to me. Once the mines are affixed, the city's lifeblood will tremble beneath my command. London will kneel. The Gentry will fall!
计划即将完成。我的泰晤士猎犬——光滑、顺从、充满潜力——已经几乎准备就绪。它们能在肮脏的河水下悄声游动，有了经过加强的挽具后也能背负更多……有说服力的货物。很快，英国的统治者和立法者就将意识到，他们以为理所当然属于自己的水域，其实属于我。等我安上地雷，这座城市的命脉将在我的掌控下颤抖。伦敦将向我臣服。绅士会将会倒台！

Damn the meddling corrupt Bobbies! A nosy Bobby caught sight of the modifications to the harnesses - he muttered something about "unnatural contraption" before I silenced him. Anyways, the Thameshound's first test was performed as perfect as I'd hoped. In their first test the mine latched perfectly to a passing barge, and in mere moments, it was matchwood. RIP to the Thameshound! But yes, the people in Eastminster are whispering now, calling it an accident. Let them believe in misfortune for now. Soon, they will believe in Morrisson.
爱管闲事的腐败条子，真该死！有个没事找事的警察发现了挽具上的改装——在我让他彻底闭嘴前，他嘟哝了句“不自然的装置”。总之，泰晤士猎犬进行的第一项测试完美结束，一如我希望的那样。在这场测试中，地雷完美固定在了一艘驶过的驳船上，这条船没过多久就成了木头碎片。安息吧，泰晤士猎犬！不过，伊斯敏斯特的人现在在聊这件事，说是意外事故。现在就让他们觉得这是不幸作祟吧。他们很快就会知道，这其实是莫里森的杰作。

Avoid the Tower at all costs. I learned this the hard way. There be some fucking mental people guarding it. Literal crazy people roam the grounds. I watched from some nearby scaffolding as they brought down some poor wretch, tore into him with the savagery of starved dogs. Ate him. I had always assumed the crows were the only ones feasting there. How wrong I was.
费劲力气才避开伦敦塔。经历了很不好的事情才知道的。那里有些神经病在守着。字面意义上的神经病，在那里走来走去。我之前从附近的脚手架上看到过他们带进来某个倒霉蛋，野蛮地把那人开膛破肚，像一群饿了三天的狗。吃了他。我总以为只有乌鸦在那里大快朵颐。真是大错特错。

日志条目21

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_RESettlerNote02 <12>
The last tin of beans is gone. The corner shops were ransacked long ago, the supermarkets stripped bare. I scavenged through a townhouse in Tower Hamlets, only to find cupboards full of fine china but not a morsel of food. The hunger gnaws at me now... fucking starving. I caught myself staring too long at a RadRat who was just there scurrying across the floorboards. Tomorrow, I may not let it go.
最后一罐豆子没了。街角的商店很久之前就被洗劫一空，超市也被扒得干干净净。我在陶尔哈姆莱茨的一个仓库里搜刮，却只找到几橱柜的上等瓷器和一点食物残渣。饥饿感现在正折磨着我……他妈的，饿死了。有只老鼠刚刚跑过地板，我发现我盯它盯得有点太久了。明天，我也许不会让它跑掉。

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_SouthwarkBermondseyRowHouse02 <5>
'''Ask and the Lord provides. We just signed our biggest contract yet. It took two months of constant interviews, but they picked our design for the London Wheel Project, and we're going to be paid hundreds of thousands of pounds for it.

Pip is overjoyed. We went out to celebrate tonight, but our favourite restaurant shut down due to the gas shortage. We had some street food, and the rain came along to send us back home.

I know we don't have the money yet, but I can't stop thinking about what this means for us.Pip mentioned we could pay for some treatments to help us conceive. I couldn't stop crying, and he thought he said something hurtful! I had to tell him it was tears of joy.

Good times are just around the corner.'''
'''老天作证，我们刚刚签下这辈子最大的一个合同。两个月不间断的面试，但他们最终还是选择了我们给伦敦轮项目提出的方案，很快就会付我们几十万英镑。

皮普欣喜若狂。我们今晚出去庆祝了一番，但我们最喜欢的餐厅却因为燃气短缺关门了。我们吃了点街头小吃，然后被雨赶回了家。

虽然知道钱还没到账上，但我还是禁不住在想，这笔钱对我们而言意味着什么。皮普说我们可以用来支付治疗费，这样就能怀孕了。我忍不住哭起来，他还以为自己说了什么伤我心的话！我告诉他，我其实是喜极而泣。

好日子就要来了。'''

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_SouthwarkBermondseyRowHouse02 <7>
'''It's official: the London Wheel Project is dead. Despite months of hard work, despite the fact we drove up to Westminster almost every day, despite the fact we took every single note, they cancelled it.

I don't understand what we did wrong. This project was going to change our lives. It was our chance to leave a mark on the London skyline, but it was also our last shot at starting a family. We simply can't avoid the treatments they've offered us at the fertility clinic.

Pip is taking it rather well, but I can feel myself sinking into my mind, just like I did back in February. I don't want to go back to that low point.

Despite our sudden lack of funds, Pip offered to take me on a holiday. I don't understand what I've done to deserve this beautiful man in my life.'''
'''官方通知：伦敦轮项目破产。哪怕我们辛苦工作了几个月，哪怕我们天天开车去威斯敏斯特，哪怕我们记录了每一个细节，他们还是取消了项目。

我不理解我们做错了什么。这个项目本会改变我们的生活，本该是我们在伦敦天际线上留名的机会，同时也是我们组成家庭的最后机会。生育诊所给的治疗方案，我们压根担负不起。

皮普很坦然地接受了，我却难以自拔，就像在今年二月的时候。我不想回到那个低谷。

尽管突然没了钱，皮普还是说要带我去度假。我不理解自己做了什么，竟然能在一生中遇上这样心善的男人。'''

'''Just when I thought things couldn't get any stranger, they do. I was about to meet a client when we got a visit from a government agent with a case. He told us this was our payment for participating in the 'London Eye's design process.'

The case was filled with at least one hundred thousand pounds. I had never seen that much money in my life, and there was even more of it.

Ever since they've started construction on the Eye, I've tried to find out whose design they went with. But the agent wouldn't tell me anything. He just kept repeating the money would 'make things good between us.' 

I think we've just been bribed. Pip is overjoyed, of course. He says it's about time we got bribed.'''
'''事情总会出人意料的发展，变得愈发奇怪。就在我打算去见客户时，一个政府的代理人提着箱子找上了我们。他说这是我们参与“伦敦眼设计过程”的报酬。

箱子里至少装着10万英镑，我这辈子都没见过那么多钱，而且这10万还只是个开头。

自伦敦眼开始建设后，我就在查他们用了谁的设计。可那位政府的代理人什么都不告诉我，只是反复地说这笔钱“对我们双方都好”。

'''It's been three weeks since we got our bribe and we have yet to spend a single pound. Pip's mother calls it decision paralysis. I think there's something much more nefarious going on here.

Ever since we received the money from that agent, I've noticed some strange things. Every morning, I see the same old woman walk up and down my street. I was in a call with a friend of mine last week, and after she hung up, I briefly heard someone else on the phone.

I told Pip I think the government is surveilling us. He doesn't understand why that's a bad thing, but he sees why I'm worried. He suggested we set some money aside for the fertility treatment, and hide the rest.

'''自被贿赂后已经过去了三周，那笔钱我们分文未动。皮普的妈妈说我们犯了选择困难症。我觉得这里面有很大的道德问题。

从那个代理人手里接过这笔钱后，我就注意到了些怪事。每天早上，我都能看到同一个老太太从我住处前的路上走过。上周我正在和朋友打电话，但是在她挂断后，我听到电话里有别人的声音。

我告诉皮普，政府可能在监视我们。他想不明白这怎么会是件坏事，但明白我为什么感到担心。他建议拿出一部分钱用于生育治疗，其他的都藏好。

我还没拿定主意。我一会儿工作，一会儿听新闻，不停来回。就在离我们房子几个街区外的地方发生了暴动。那里发生了什么？'''

'''Well, bach, things have gone a bit south, haven't they? Supplies are runnin' low, and I mean properly low. We've been scroungin' for scraps like rats in the gutters, but there's only so much you can find in this bleedin' wasteland. Word's been goin' around, too - people sayin' to steer clear of the place. No clue how that got out, but it's made things even tougher. Used to be, we could get a bit of a haul from there when times got rough, but now it's like everyone's too scared to even look our way. Bloody madness, that is.

Caught some of the lads actin' right dodgy the other day. Thought I was seein' things, but no, there they were, huddled in a corner, takin' cheeky nibbles off one of the corpses. Now, I've seen a lot in my time, but that? That's a step too far, even for this lot. Had to put 'em down myself. Didn't want to, but what can you do? Can't have the whole gang turnin' to that kind of behaviour, or next thing you know, we'll be pickin' each other off one by one.

But then, I've been thinkin', see? Maybe... maybe we're fightin' against the tide... What if we just gave in? I mean, think about it. If we all became cannibals like 'em Beefeaters, we wouldn't have to worry about food no more, would we? Plenty of meat around, though not the kind you'd want to write home about.

But here's the thing, once you start eatin' what's around, you stop carin'. You go a bit daft, aye, but maybe that's for the best. A bit of madness might be just what we need to survive this mess. No worries about right or wrong, no fear of what's comin'. Just do what you have to, and don't think twice about it.

Maybe we're all headed that way anyway, slowly but surely. This life? It drives you mad, day by day, bit by bit. Why not embrace it? At least if we all go... "Beefeaterish", we'll have a plan, well, as much of a plan as we've ever had.

Still, somethin' about it feels off, doesn't it? Like we're losin' whatever little shred of humanity we've got left. But then again, what's the point of holdin' onto that when it doesn't get you anywhere? Food's food, after all. Trust me, I know.

Maybe I'll sit on it for a bit, see where the wind blows. Who knows, maybe this is the way forward. Can't get much fatter after all, heh.

Anyway, enough chatter for now. I gotta see if there's anything left in the fridge worth takin' before the next bunch of fools wander in 'n steal my snacks.'''
'''唉，事情变得有点糟糕了，不是吗？补给快要见底，一点都不剩的那种。我们就像排水沟里的老鼠似的到处找细碎，但这片天杀的废土上就那么点东西。还有谣言说，大家以后都要避开这里走。我想不出事情怎么会变成这样，但情况反正是更糟了。以前哪怕景况不佳，我们也能多少捞点，但现在大家好像连看一眼我们这儿都会被吓的不敢来似的。真是疯了。

前几天，几个小伙子做坏事的时候被我逮了个正着。我以为自己看花眼了，但事实就是如此：他们几个人缩在角落里，小口吃着一具尸体上的肉。我这辈子见过很多事情，但即使对这几个人而言，吃尸体也实在是越界太多。我没办法，只能亲自解决他们。我本不想这样，但我又有什么选择？不能让整个帮派的人都变成那样，不然他们现在吃的是别人，下次就会对着自己人一个个地下手了。

但我也一直在思考，也许……我们一直在和这个世界的规则作对……要是我们直接放弃挣扎，会怎么样？想象一下，如果我们都变成了牛堡塔卫那样的食人者，就不用再担心食物了，不是吗？附近那么多肉可以吃，尽管都不是能写在信上告诉家里人的肉。

不过关键在于，在吃了第一口后，你就会吃第二口、第三口，不再关心吃的是谁。没错，你会变得疯癫一些，但也许这才是最好的活法。为了在这个一团糟的世界里活下来，一点疯癫可能正是我们需要的。不再担心是非对错，不再害怕会有报应。如果不得不做，那就放手去做，不再反复思考和犹豫。

也许，我们最终都会走上食人的路，只是时间问题罢了。这样的生活会让你变成疯子，一天天，一点点得让你发疯。既然如此，为何不欣然接受？我们如果都开始……过牛堡塔卫式的生活，至少还有过日子的规划，呵，和曾经的对生活的规划一样。

但即使这样说，我总觉得有点不对劲，不是吗？就好像我们本就不多的那点人性彻底消失了一样。但要是看不到出路，又何必有所顾忌和保留？食物就是食物，人总归得吃。信我，我是个明白人。

我大概会在这里继续坐一会儿，再思考思考。谁知道呢，也许这才是走下去的正道。反正我也胖不到哪里去了，哈。

总之，闲聊得多了。我得去看看冰箱里还有什么值得拿的，免得下一批蠢货溜进来偷我的零食吃。'''

'''Hi Baird, I finally got those sales reports collated for the quarterly meeting; officially, it’s not looking great.

Simply put, people aren’t really buying tellies anymore. With the way rationing is going, it’s getting harder (and most importantly, more expensive) to get hold of a crappy TV - let alone a good one - and then that means we have to bump up the prices of our stock accordingly. That however has the knock-on effect of making the shite we sell too expensive for your average Joe Public to afford, and those who can still afford something good like a Kenley set (and not have to worry about whether or not they can eat for the next 3 months) aren’t going to risk lugging their set down to us when they probably have someone on call that’ll go to them directly.

Another thing - People aren’t buying TVs anymore (I think) in part because they simply just don’t want to see what’s going on in the world right now. I mean, the only real channel available (and indeed the only one that’s worth watching at present) is the BBM, and all that’s been shown there is news about the ever-worsening conflict in Europe, civil unrest and everything either running out or getting more expensive. Not the most appealing thing to watch with your tea, no.

I guess there is somewhat of a silver lining to this though. Though our TV sales have gone through the floor, I’ve noticed a slight increase in sales of home-radios and music players. Not great, but not terrible either - at least enough to take note of, I guess. Chalking this up to either people not wanting to see the end of the world hurtling towards them in their front rooms, or they’d rather drown it out with some good tunes.

Either way though, we’re basically fucked for meeting the next sales quota. Happy times!'''
'''嗨，贝尔德，我终于搞到了为季度会议整理的销售报告。官方点说，情况并不乐观。

'''Subject: Initial Observations

The feral ghoul population in London has surged over the past few months. This sudden increase has piqued my curiosity, prompting me to investigate the underlying causes. Preliminary observations suggest a connection between the feral ghouls and the radiation hotspots scattered throughout the city. It seems these areas serve as breeding grounds for the ghouls, attracting them in large numbers. I intend to delve deeper into this phenomenon and determine if there are specific factors that contribute to their proliferation.

Further study is needed to map out these hotspots accurately and assess their radiation levels. I will also need to examine the behaviour of the feral ghouls in relation to these areas. Are they drawn to the radiation, or is it merely a byproduct of their presence? My next steps will involve setting up observation posts and collecting samples from both the environment and the ghouls themselves.

- Director Herbertson'''
'''主题：伦敦狂尸鬼数量

过去的几个月中，伦敦狂尸鬼数量急速增长。这一突增现象引起了我的好奇，让我立即着手调查其背后原因。初步观察结果表明，狂尸鬼与分散全城的辐射热点区域有关。这些区域似乎是孕育尸鬼的地方，能吸引大批尸鬼前往。我打算更深入地调查这一现象，查明导致它们数量增长的具体原因。

为了准确标记热点区域的位置，估测其辐射等级，我需要进一步研究。同时，我还需要测试狂尸鬼的行为与这些区域的关联。是它们被辐射热点吸引而来，还是它们的聚集产生了辐射热点？下一步我将设置观察站点，收集环境和尸鬼自身的样本。'''

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_ABCWLab <4>
'''Subject: Behavioural Patterns of Feral Ghouls

After several weeks of monitoring, I have begun to identify certain behavioural patterns in the feral ghouls. They appear to be most active during the night, possibly to avoid the residual UV radiation during daylight hours. Their movement patterns are erratic but seem to follow a consistent routine when observed over a longer period. The ghouls often congregate near radiation hotspots and scavenge for 'food' (People) in nearby areas. I hypothesise that these locations offer some form of sustenance or safety, though the exact reasons remain unclear?

Further research will focus on the specific triggers of these behaviours and whether external factors, such as weather or human activity, influence their actions. Understanding these patterns is crucial for developing strategies to manage and possibly mitigate the feral ghoul threat in London.

- Director Herbertson'''
'''主题：狂尸鬼行为模式

经过几周的密切观察后，我已经能辨识出狂尸鬼的特定行为模式。它们在夜间最为活跃，可能是为了避开白天时段被紫外线照射。它们拥有奇怪的活动模式，但如果放在较长的时间尺度上看，它们似乎遵循着一条一致的模式。尸鬼通常会聚集在辐射热点附近，从周边区域中搜刮食物。我姑且假设这些地点存在某种维生物质或能提供安全，但具体原因仍不明晰。

之后的研究将重点关注这些行为的具体诱因，以及天气或人类活动等外界因素是否会影响它们的行为。只有理解这些模式，我们才能制定战略，控制伦敦城中狂尸鬼带来的威胁，甚至可能减少这类威胁。'''

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_SouthwarkUBHQ06_Sub03 <3>
On the Beauty of Wheels (draft 1)
论轮之美（草稿1）

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_SouthwarkUBHQ06_Sub03 <4>
Dear members of the board, I come before you as a humbled engineer. Despite our countless years attempting to develop robotic transportation systems that simulate our two human legs, we have yet to successfully complete a robot capable of using said legs without walking into a wall, off a cliff, or both at the same time. That is why I propose we switch to a wheel-based system for all further prototypes. I believe our mistake was looking towards humans for inspiration, as opposed to machines. And is the wheel not the most elegant of machines? Did the wheel not give birth to all of human progress and civilization? Consider the wheel, members of the board, and how its beauty can in turn make our products more beautiful.
各位尊敬的董事会成员，来到你们面前的，是一介卑微的工程师。尽管我们曾花费无数年月改进模拟人腿的机器人运输系统，但却始终未能完成一个能够驾驭这双腿，不会再撞到墙上，掉下悬崖，或者既撞上墙又掉下悬崖的机器人。因此我提议，在未来的原型机中，使用以轮子为基础的系统。我认为我们的问题亟需人类的灵感来解答，而非指望机器。而轮子，难道不是机器中最优雅的吗？难道人类所有的进步与文明，不是自轮子中诞生的吗？尊敬的董事会成员们，考虑一下轮子吧。想想看，它的美能让我们的产品更加动人。

> TERM.ITXT Folon_TERM_SouthwarkUBHQ06_Sub03 <5>
The Simplicity of Wheels (draft 2)
轮之简（草稿2）

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_SouthwarkUBHQ06_Sub03 <6>
Members of the board, as Chief Engineer, I am ready to stake my reputation and further employment on the following idea: that wheels need us more than we need them. Whilst we could easily develop working robotic legs within the next decade, we've come to realise through careful market research that there is a fantastic opportunity waiting for us here. If we add wheels to our robots, not only can we take advantage of surprisingly low prices on materials and construction, but we can also revolutionise our industry, adopting a new paradigm and showing everyone how cavemen got it right all those millions of years ago. Consider the wheel, members of the board, and how its simplicity can in turn make our products more simple.

March Entry:
三月的条目：

> TERM.UNAM Folon_TERM_WandsworthRetrofittingCentre07 <6>
'''I cannot believe that I have been conscripted into the army and assigned to work at a government retrofitting centre. 8 months I'm to be stationed here!

I guess it feels like a cruel twist of fate to be tasked with confiscating the fusion cell and fusion core technology from London residents, who have invested so much time and money in these rare and expensive technologies.

Hell, even as I arrived at the centre, I was met with angry residents who were protesting the government's decision to take away their fusion-powered cars. It breaks my heart to see their disappointment and frustration, knowing that they have no say in the matter.

Throughout the day, we all worked tirelessly to retrofit these cars with old-style gas engines. The once-sleek and modern vehicles are now clunky and outdated, emitting harmful emissions into the air. The irony is not lost on me; we are supposed to be fighting a war to save our planet, yet we are actively contributing to its destruction.'''
'''难以置信，我竟然参了军，还被分配到政府的一个翻新中心工作。我要在这驻扎整整8个月！

被安排去从伦敦居民手上征收核聚变电池和核心，我猜这种命运的转折放谁身上都不好受，毕竟他们在这项稀有且昂贵的技术产品上已经投入了那么多的时间和金钱，如今却要接受这样残酷的安排。

淦，甚至在到中心的时候，我都看到有生气的居民在抗议政府没收他们由核聚变核心驱动的汽车的决定。看到他们这样绝望和沮丧我也很伤心，而且我深知，他们在这件事上没有话语权。

我们从早到晚都在把那些车改造成用老式汽油引擎的款式，大家一刻也不得闲。这些曾经线条流畅，走在时代最前沿的载具如今不仅笨重不堪，和时代严重脱轨，还会向空气排放有害气体。这句讽刺的话我现在都还记得：我们本该为保护地球而战，现在却一门心思地在加速它的毁灭。'''

我还在努力挣扎，想在我对国家的使命以及我对这些人的同情之间找到平衡点。逼着这些人放弃他们珍爱的东西让我觉得自己背叛了人民，尤其是在现在这种情况下，战争连一点结束的征兆都没有。'''

一个男人开着自己的车过来，但他却并不想放弃这辆车。他说这是他唯一的交通工具，他没钱再买一辆新车。而当我们坚持要拆解掉时，他开始大喊大叫，人也疯了起来。好几个士兵过来才把他压制住，但他却唤醒了我。

我从没想过这件事会怎样深刻影响到人们的生活。这不仅仅是没了一辆车那么简单，这是让大家失去独立，自由，还有稳定的财务状况。我忍不住去想是不是还有别的方法能打赢这场仗而不用夺走老百姓的生计。'''

格雷先生声称，当晚7点50分，两名男子来到酒吧。格雷先生对他们的描述如下：这两名男子名为“马库斯”和“耶利米”，均年约三十岁，头戴平顶帽，身着外套。格雷先生形容两人“散发着恶臭”。他指出两人具有印度血统，但其推断依据仅包含前述气味以及他自称的种族辨识能力。

我问格雷先生，他的投诉是否与涉事人员的种族背景有关，他坚称毫无关联。随后他向我叙述了以下遭遇：马库斯和耶利米询问正在照看酒吧的格雷先生，他的酒吧是什么样子的。格雷先生没听懂这个问题。据格雷先生所述，耶利米随后“俯身越过柜台，向我展示他[脏话]兔子纹身”。耶利米询问格雷先生是否和他们是一伙人，格雷先生表示困惑。

格雷先生试图让两人离开，但两人拒绝并坐到了离洗手间最近的卡座里。格雷先生告诉我他“一直盯着他们”，但“他们除了[脏话]盯着[脏话]从[脏话]厕所里出来的[脏话]人外，没做什么别的。” 我意识到格雷先生的投诉可能不值得深究，便询问他是否目睹任何违法行为。格雷先生表示未发现任何违法行为的具体事例。

为了完成工作，我请格雷先生继续讲述后续经过。格雷先生说，那两人仅坐了两分钟便起身离去。据格雷先生，耶利米随后在门口停下，回头对他说要写信给当地报纸“揭露我[指格雷先生]的无能”，随即离去。我追问他所谓“无能”的具体含义，但格雷先生却以满口脏话的咆哮回应，大谈他的社会学看法。

我已完整听取格雷先生关于此次遭遇的陈述，以及他对名为马库斯和耶利米两位人士的描述。建议不再理会格雷先生就此特定事项的任何来电。据我判断，此二人正是事件报告#2300中提及的当事人。'''

Upon arrival at 22:45, I approached the area on foot to avoid startling the individuals. I observed two suspects, later identified as Jimmy Doe and Janie Smith, engaged in sexual intercourse in a public place. Both individuals were partially undressed and did not immediately notice my presence.

- Jimmy Doe: Admitted to the act, stating it was a "spur-of-the-moment decision" and expressed regret for the public indecency.
